Laws, Energy, Rotation, and Gravitation • Core Physics • Advanced Physics • Research Lanes
Gravitation • Analytical Mechanics • Plasma and Astrophysics • High Energy and Cosmology
Compare orbital speed, escape speed, and orbital period around a planet.
Gravity supplies centripetal force for circular orbit; escape speed is sqrt(2) times orbital speed at the same radius.
Escape speed is greater than circular orbital speed at the same orbital radius.
How can we use satellite orbit and escape speed to predict radius before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect radius data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.
Visualize how gravitational force changes with mass and distance.
Every mass attracts every other mass. The force is proportional to both masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance.
Planet mass • Test mass • Distance scale • Field map
Doubling distance reduces gravitational force to one-fourth, if masses are unchanged.
How can we use universal gravitation field map to predict mass 2 before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect mass 2 data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.
Visualize sinusoidal emf generated by rotating a coil in a magnetic field.
Changing magnetic flux through a rotating coil induces emf. For uniform rotation, emf varies sinusoidally.
Rotating coil • Bar magnets • Slip rings • AC graph
Peak emf increases with turns, field, area, and angular speed.
How can we use ac generator to predict magnetic field before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect magnetic field data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.
Compare reactance, impedance, current, and resonance in a series LCR circuit.
At resonance, inductive and capacitive reactances cancel and current is maximum.
AC source • Resistor • Inductor • Capacitor • Ammeter
Current peaks when inductive and capacitive reactances are equal.
How can we use ac lcr resonance to predict frequency before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect frequency data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.
Electric Charges, Fields, Potential, and Capacitance
Calculate charge and stored energy for a capacitor and compare combinations.
A capacitor stores charge with Q = CV and energy U = 1/2 CV^2.
Energy grows with the square of voltage.
How can we use capacitor energy and combination to predict voltage before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect voltage data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.
Compare emf, terminal voltage, current, and internal resistance of a cell.
A real cell has internal resistance, so terminal voltage falls as current increases: V = E - Ir.
Terminal voltage decreases when load current increases.
How can we use cell internal resistance to predict external r before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect external r data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.
Model electrolysis/electroplating as charge passing through a conducting solution.
Conducting liquids allow current through ions; deposited material depends on current and time.
More current and longer time produce more deposited material.
How can we use chemical effects of current to predict time before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect time data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.
Connect circuit power to electrical energy consumed over time.
Power is the rate of electrical energy use; P = VI and energy equals power times time.
Battery • Bulb • Ammeter • Voltmeter • Energy meter
Energy consumed increases with both power rating and usage time.
How can we use electric power and energy to predict current before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect current data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.
Electric Charges, Fields, Potential, and Capacitance • Electrodynamics
Compare electric field and potential around point charges.
Electric field is force per unit charge, while potential is work per unit charge.
Point charges • Electric field region • Probe
Field follows inverse square with distance; potential follows inverse distance.
How can we use electrostatic field and potential to predict distance before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect distance data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.
Explore induced emf from changing magnetic flux.
Faraday's law says induced emf equals the negative rate of change of magnetic flux linkage.
Faster flux change and more turns produce larger induced emf.
How can we use faraday induction to predict flux change before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect flux change data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.

Explore how current, resistance, and time affect Joule heating.
Electrical heating follows H = I^2Rt, so current has the strongest effect.
Doubling current makes heating four times larger for the same resistance and time.
How can we use heating effect of current to predict current before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect current data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.
Use junction and loop rules to analyse a two-resistor network.
Charge conservation gives junction rule, and energy conservation gives loop rule.
At a junction, incoming current equals outgoing current.
How can we use kirchhoff circuit rules to predict r1 before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect r1 data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.
Find an unknown resistance using the balanced Wheatstone bridge relation.
At balance, no current flows through the galvanometer and R/X = l/(100-l).
Meter bridge • Known resistor • Unknown resistor • Galvanometer • Jockey
How can we use meter bridge to predict balance length before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect balance length data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.

Plot voltage against current and determine resistance from the graph slope.
For an ohmic conductor at constant temperature, V is directly proportional to I.
The V-I graph is a straight line through origin for an ohmic conductor.
How can we use ohm's law v-i graph to predict resistance before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect resistance data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.

Series and Parallel Resistance • Current Electricity
Compare equivalent resistance and current in series and parallel circuits.
Series resistances add; parallel conductances add.
Parallel equivalent resistance is less than each individual branch resistance.
How can we use series and parallel resistance to predict r2 before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect r2 data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.

Static Electricity and Lightning • Electric Charges, Fields, Potential, and Capacitance
Explore attraction, repulsion, and the distance dependence of electric force.
Like charges repel, unlike charges attract, and electric force follows an inverse-square relation.
Like charges repel, unlike charges attract, and force reduces rapidly with distance.
How can we use static electricity and lightning to predict charge 2 before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect charge 2 data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.
Compare primary and secondary voltages, current, and efficiency in a transformer.
An ideal transformer follows Vs/Vp = Ns/Np. Practical transformers lose some energy as heat and magnetic leakage.
AC source • Primary coil • Secondary coil • Iron core • Load
More secondary turns than primary turns steps voltage up.
How can we use transformer lab to predict np before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect np data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.

Build truth tables for NOT, AND, OR, NAND, and NOR gates.
Logic gates convert binary inputs into binary outputs and form the building blocks of digital electronics.
Switch inputs • Logic gate • LED output • Truth table
Each gate follows its standard truth table; NAND and NOR invert AND and OR outputs.
How can we use logic gates to predict input a before reading the answer?

A p-n junction conducts strongly after cut-in voltage in forward bias and blocks most reverse current.
Forward current flows only when input exceeds diode drop; reverse half-cycle is blocked in half-wave rectification.
How can we use semiconductor diode and rectifier to predict diode drop before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect diode drop data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.
Compare renewable and conventional energy sources using power output, efficiency, cost, and environmental score.
A good energy source is available, economical, efficient, easy to store/transport, and has low environmental impact.
Energy dashboard • Efficiency meter • Impact meter • Load bulb
Higher efficiency increases useful output, while fossil-fuel-heavy mixes raise impact score.
How can we use sources of energy comparator to predict input energy before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect input energy data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.

Explore pressure-speed-height tradeoffs in streamline fluid flow.
For ideal flow, pressure energy, kinetic energy per volume, and gravitational potential per volume remain conserved along a streamline.

Higher flow speed or height leaves less static pressure in the same streamline.
How can we use bernoulli fluid flow to predict speed before reading the answer?

Motion, Force, and Work • Matter, Thermal Physics, Oscillations, and Waves
Floatation and Buoyancy • Solids and Fluids
Compare floating and sinking using Archimedes' principle.
An immersed object experiences an upward force equal to the weight of displaced fluid.
Fluid region • Wood block • Steel block
Wood tends to float in water, while steel sinks.
How can we use buoyancy to predict density before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect density data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.
Predict whether an object floats or sinks by comparing object density with liquid density.
An object floats if its average density is less than the fluid density, and sinks if it is greater.
Fluid tank • Test block • Density slider • Submerged fraction meter
Objects less dense than the fluid float partially submerged; denser objects sink.
How can we use density float-or-sink tank to predict object density before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect object density data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.
Force and Pressure • Matter, Thermal Physics, Oscillations, and Waves

Observe how liquid pressure changes with density and depth.
Gauge pressure in a liquid is rho gh, so it grows linearly with depth.
Fluid tank • Depth marker • Pressure gauge
Pressure rises linearly as the sensor moves deeper.
How can we use fluid pressure with depth to predict density before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect density data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.

Compare pressure from force over area and pressure due to liquid depth.
Pressure is force per unit area; liquid pressure also increases with depth.
Block • Fluid region • Pressure gauge • Ruler

A coil carrying current produces a magnetic field; an iron core concentrates the field.

More turns, more current, and a stronger core produce a stronger electromagnet.
How can we use electromagnet to predict current before reading the answer?

A charge moving perpendicular to a magnetic field experiences force qvB and follows circular motion.
Force increases linearly with charge, speed, and magnetic field strength.

Build a small reproducible physics workflow: choose a model, step size, uncertainty, graph, and verification rule.

Compare left and right forces and predict whether an object stays still, moves steadily, or accelerates.

Net force and acceleration: F_{net}=F_R-F_L,\quad a=\frac{F_{net}}{m}

Calculate work done and power for a force moving an object through a displacement.
Work is energy transferred by force through displacement; power is work done per unit time.
Work and power: W = Fs,\quad P = \frac{W}{t}
The same work done in less time gives greater power.

Hydrogen atom model • Energy level chart • Spectrum viewer

Electron source • Accelerating plates • Diffraction screen
Higher accelerating voltage gives shorter de Broglie wavelength.

Radioactive nuclei decay randomly, but large samples follow N = N0(1/2)^(t/T).
After each half-life, half the remaining undecayed nuclei are left.

Electron kinetic energy equals photon energy minus metal work function when frequency exceeds threshold.
Photoelectric tube • Light source • Retarding voltage
Intensity changes photocurrent, while frequency controls maximum kinetic energy.
How can we use photoelectric equation to predict work function before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect work function data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.
Explore time dilation, length contraction, and relativistic energy using a light-clock and spacetime graph.
At speeds close to light speed, observers can disagree on measured time and length while the spacetime interval remains consistent.
Light clock • Velocity slider • Spacetime graph • Energy readout
As speed approaches light speed, gamma rises, measured time dilates, and energy demand grows sharply.
How can we use special relativity bridge to predict gamma before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect gamma data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.
Natural Phenomena • Optics and Modern Physics

Trace refraction through a rectangular glass slab and calculate refraction angle.
A ray bends towards the normal on entering glass and away from the normal on leaving, emerging parallel with lateral shift.
Light ray • Glass slab • Protractor • Screen
The emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray but laterally shifted.
How can we use glass slab refraction to predict refractive index before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect refractive index data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.
Model image formation on the retina and correction of myopia and hypermetropia.

The cornea and eye lens converge incoming light so a sharp image forms on the retina. In myopia, distant-object rays focus before the retina and a concave lens spreads them before they enter the eye. In hypermetropia, nearby-object rays would focus behind the retina and a convex lens adds convergence.
Realistic cutaway eye model • Retina screen • Concave corrective lens • Convex corrective lens • Ray overlay
Myopia is corrected by a concave lens; hypermetropia is corrected by a convex lens. A clear image forms when the corrected ray focus lies on the retina.
How can we use human eye and vision defects to predict far point/near point before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect far point/near point data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.

Object outside focus gives real image; object inside focus gives virtual image.

Trace incident, refracted, and emergent rays through a prism, then compare deviation, minimum deviation, and colour dispersion.
A prism refracts light at two faces. Since refractive index is slightly larger for shorter wavelengths, violet bends more than red and white light spreads into VIBGYOR.
Approximate deviation: \delta \approx (n-1)A • Minimum deviation: n=\frac{\sin((A+D_m)/2)}{\sin(A/2)} • Snell at prism faces: \sin i=n\sin r_1,\ r_1+r_2=A,\ n\sin r_2=\sin e

For a plane mirror, incidence angle equals reflection angle and image distance equals object distance.
How can we use reflection by plane mirror to predict incidence angle before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect incidence angle data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.
Light, Shadows, and Reflection • Reflection by Mirrors
Show rectilinear propagation of light using shadows, umbra, penumbra, and eclipses.
Light travels in straight lines. Extended sources produce umbra and penumbra regions behind an opaque object.
Light source • Opaque ball • Screen • Distance scale
A smaller source gives a sharper shadow; an extended source creates penumbra around the umbra.
How can we use shadows and eclipses to predict object distance before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect object distance data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.
Find critical angle and show when light reflects completely inside a denser medium.
Total internal reflection occurs when light travels from denser to rarer medium and incidence angle exceeds the critical angle.
Glass block • Ray source • Protractor • Screen
For glass to air, angles greater than the critical angle produce total internal reflection.
How can we use total internal reflection to predict n2 before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect n2 data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.
Matter, Thermal Physics, Oscillations, and Waves
Compare a simple oscillator with a double-pendulum style coupled oscillator and identify the start of chaotic motion.
Coupled nonlinear oscillators can become sensitive to initial conditions, so tiny angle changes can grow into visibly different phase paths.
Double pendulum • Phase plot • Angle sliders • Energy tracker
Small angles stay regular for longer, while larger coupled motion separates quickly and produces complex phase paths.
How can we use chaotic and coupled oscillators to predict angle 2 before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect angle 2 data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.
Mix hot and cold water samples and predict the final equilibrium temperature.
In an insulated mixture, heat lost by the hot body is approximately equal to heat gained by the cold body.
Calorimeter • Hot water • Cold water • Thermometer
The final temperature lies between the hot and cold initial temperatures and shifts toward the larger heat capacity sample.
How can we use calorimetry mixing lab to predict hot temp before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect hot temp data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.
Matter, Thermal Physics, Oscillations, and Waves • Core Physics • Research Lanes
Thermal Properties and Thermodynamics • Kinetic Theory • Statistical and Thermal Physics • Biophysics and Complex Systems
Use the ideal gas law to connect pressure, volume, temperature, and amount of gas.
Ideal gas pressure comes from molecular collisions and follows PV = nRT.
At fixed n, pressure rises with temperature and falls as volume increases.
How can we use gas laws and kinetic theory to predict temperature before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect temperature data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.
Compare temperature scales and estimate heat needed to change the temperature of a body.
Temperature measures hotness, while heat is energy transferred because of a temperature difference.
Thermometer • Water sample • Heat source • Temperature scale
Kelvin rises one-to-one with Celsius, and heat needed increases with mass and specific heat.
How can we use heat and temperature to predict temperature before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect temperature data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.

Transfer of Heat • Thermal Properties and Thermodynamics • Statistical and Thermal Physics
Visualize conduction and estimate heat flow through materials of different thickness.
Conduction transfers heat faster through high-conductivity, large-area, thin materials.
Conduction bar • Thermometer • Heat source • Insulator sample
Heat rate increases with conductivity and area, and decreases with thickness.
How can we use heat transfer to predict area before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect area data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.
Compare microstates, ensemble averages, phase tendency, and transport response without long derivations.
Statistical mechanics connects many microscopic configurations to macroscopic quantities such as temperature, pressure, entropy, and fluctuations.
Particle ensemble • Temperature dial • Phase map • Distribution graph
Higher temperature broadens the energy distribution and increases average kinetic energy and fluctuations.
How can we use statistical ensemble lab to predict particles before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect particles data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.
Matter, Thermal Physics, Oscillations, and Waves • Core Physics
Thermal Properties and Thermodynamics • Statistical and Thermal Physics
Compare isothermal, isobaric, and isochoric process work and heat trends.
Work done by a gas is the area under the PV curve, with different constraints for different processes.
Isochoric work is zero, while isobaric work equals pressure times volume change.
How can we use thermodynamic processes to predict delta volume before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect delta volume data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.
Friction, Sound, and Light • Matter, Thermal Physics, Oscillations, and Waves
Sound • Oscillations and Waves • Resonance and Forced Oscillations
Visualize standing-wave nodal patterns on a vibrating plate.
Sand gathers along nodes where the plate has minimal vibration.
Higher resonant frequencies produce more complex nodal patterns.
How can we use chladni plate to predict frequency before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect frequency data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.
Use echo timing to estimate distance or sound speed.
An echo is reflected sound; the measured time is for the sound to travel to the reflector and back.
Sound source • Wall • Stopwatch • Temperature control
Distance to the reflector is half the sound travel distance.
How can we use echo and speed of sound to predict temperature before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect temperature data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.
Optics and Modern Physics • Advanced Physics
Relate wavelength, frequency, energy, and common EM spectrum bands.
All electromagnetic waves travel at c in vacuum and satisfy c = f lambda.
Spectrum viewer • Frequency slider • Wavelength scale
Higher frequency means shorter wavelength and higher photon energy.
How can we use electromagnetic spectrum to predict wavelength before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect wavelength data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.
Visualize compressions, rarefactions, wavelength, frequency, amplitude, and speed of sound.
Sound in air is a longitudinal pressure wave. Particles oscillate back and forth while energy travels through the medium.
For fixed sound speed, higher frequency gives shorter wavelength.
How can we use longitudinal sound wave to predict amplitude before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect amplitude data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.
Optics and Modern Physics • Core Physics
Use two polarizers to verify Malus' law for transmitted light intensity.
Plane polarized light passing through an analyzer has intensity I = I0 cos^2(theta).
Light source • Polarizer • Analyzer • Intensity meter
Intensity is maximum at 0 degrees and near zero at 90 degrees.
How can we use polarization lab to predict analyzer angle before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect analyzer angle data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.
Optics and Modern Physics • Core Physics
Observe diffraction through a single slit.
A barrier with a narrow opening spreads an incoming wavefront into a diffraction pattern.
Narrower slits create wider spreading behind the barrier.
How can we use single slit diffraction to predict gap width before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect gap width data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.
Relate frequency to pitch, amplitude to loudness, and wavelength to wave speed.
Pitch depends on frequency, loudness depends on amplitude and intensity, and wavelength equals speed divided by frequency.
Wave source • Audio oscillator • Graph plotter
Higher frequency gives higher pitch; higher amplitude gives louder sound.
How can we use sound pitch and loudness to predict amplitude before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect amplitude data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.
Matter, Thermal Physics, Oscillations, and Waves
Oscillations and Waves • Simple Harmonic Motion - Pendulum and Spring • Resonance and Forced Oscillations
Study simple harmonic motion of a spring-mass oscillator.
For small oscillations, angular frequency is sqrt(k/m), independent of amplitude.
Increasing mass increases period; increasing spring constant decreases period.
How can we use spring-mass shm to predict mass before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect mass data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.
Friction, Sound, and Light • Motion, Force, and Work • Matter, Thermal Physics, Oscillations, and Waves • Optics and Modern Physics
Sound • Oscillations and Waves • Wave Optics
Observe interference from two coherent point wave sources.
Two in-phase sources generate constructive and destructive interference where path differences align or oppose phase.
Stable interference bands form between two coherent sources.
How can we use wave lab to predict frequency before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect frequency data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.
Optics and Modern Physics • Core Physics
Measure fringe width in a two-slit interference pattern.
Coherent light from two slits creates bright and dark fringes with beta = lambda D / d.
Fringe width increases with wavelength and screen distance, and decreases with slit separation.
How can we use young's double slit to predict screen distance before reading the answer?
A strong learner can write a prediction, collect screen distance data, explain the trend, and apply it to a new case.
